static_traits.name: Lin Jiayi
static_traits.family_status: Lives alone; grandparents have passed away
static_traits.social_status: Lacking social support to confide in (no one to comfortably discuss feelings with); interpersonal relationships not disclosed
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems before; not yet received psychotherapy; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, high cooperativeness, capable of self-reflection; harsh self-evaluation, high negative-emotion intensity (8-9/10); positive attitude, willing to try new strategies

basic_info.main_problem: Whenever I miss an episode of my favorite anime, I feel I am the 'worst fan in history', falling into strong self-criticism and negative emotions; in recent weeks this has become stronger and affects the enjoyment of watching the program.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize self-criticism is affecting my enjoyment of the things I love, and I hope to receive counseling support to change these automatic negative thoughts.
growth_experiences: Grandparents have passed away, now living alone; lacking a support system with whom to discuss feelings.

core_beliefs: I am the worst fan in history

special_situations.event: Missing an episode of a favorite anime
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I miss an episode, I am not a true fan
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constraining herself from missing again through harsh self-criticism
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am the worst fan in history

special_situations.event: Comparing with other fans, seeing them never miss episodes and always stay up to date
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only by being as perfect as others or even better does one count as a qualified fan
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly comparing herself with others to monitor and evaluate self-worth
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as they are / I am not a true fan

special_situations.event: After missing an episode, sets 'should/must' standards for self
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I must stay up to date at all times, absolutely must not miss any, or I am unqualified
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forcing herself to maintain standards with 'should / must' self-demands
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should be better at following up on these programs

special_situations.event: When noticing a plot point they had missed, focusing only on the negative and ignoring the facts that it can still be caught up on and that they still love it
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once a flaw appears, all positives no longer count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Negating positive evidence, maintaining negative self-labels to drive self-improvement
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I do not deserve to enjoy this work

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen as a 'true / qualified fan', gaining recognition and self-worth
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being defined as not good enough or 'not a true fan', and therefore belittled or excluded
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of control and 'qualification standards' through harsh self-demands and self-blame, to avoid being seen as unqualified

object_relations.self_representation: An unqualified self, prone to failure (unqualified once an episode is missed)
object_relations.object_representation: Perfect others / fan community that tolerates no mistakes (always staying up to date)

manifestations: Living alone, grandparents deceased; no suitable person to discuss feelings and troubles with
outcomes: Intensified self-criticism and heightened negative emotions; decreased ability to enjoy things

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Harsher standards for oneself than for friends
Frequent self-blame ('I am the worst fan')
Tightly binds self-worth to whether an episode was missed

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: 'Should / must' self-demands ('I should keep up with my show better')
Taking the rule 'missing an episode = not a true fan' directly as an absolute standard

positive_force: Positive attitude; willing to try new strategies and seek professional support
Having self-reflection ability, can examine and restructure evidence (can recognize friends miss episodes too)
Passionate about beloved things; willing to improve the experience
negative_force: Comparing oneself with others leads to self-deprecation
Weak social support, lacking someone to confide in

target_behavior.behavior: Strong self-criticism and negative emotions when missing an episode
antecedent: Missing an episode of a favorite anime
Comparing with other fans' perfect episode-chasing
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalized strict fan standards and all-or-nothing / overgeneralization cognitive patterns, equating one missed catch with complete failure
target_behavior.function: Maintaining and reinforcing the introjected 'qualified fan' standard through self-blame, trying to force herself never to miss again
target_behavior.consequence: Viewing experience damaged, mood markedly lowered with persistent self-criticism, further eroding enjoyment of the show
